The evidence explicitly states that "Two-dimensional transthoracic strain analysis disclosed borderline systolic impairment and hypokinetic foci in the inferolateral region." Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) with strain analysis is an echocardiographic study. The finding of "hypokinetic foci" corresponds to **Segmental wall motion abnormalities** (Option 3). Additionally, "borderline systolic impairment" indicates a functional abnormality of the left ventricle, which falls under **New focal or diffuse left or right ventricular function abnormalities** (Option 2), as strain analysis assesses myocardial deformation and function. The follow-up echocardiogram showed normalization, confirming these were new findings at presentation. There is no mention of ventricular dilation, wall thickness changes, or pericardial fluid/inflammation on the ECHO itself (CMR showed inflammation/edema, but the question asks about ECHO findings specifically). Therefore, options 2 and 3 are supported by the text describing the initial echocardiographic assessment.
